reason: M8 is a diode-connected NMOS that likely just provides a local bias reference/sink for IB1; if IB1 is already driven by an ideal/external bias source, removing M8 usually won’t change the signal-path behavior. Caveat: if IB1 is generated/stabilized on-chip using M8, deleting it can leave IB1 floating and break multiple branches.
impact_estimate: Low if IB1 is externally defined; high if IB1 depends on M8

reason: M15 appears to be part of a bias-conditioning branch that sets net043 (which then biases the auxiliary differential pair M19/M20); if net043 is supplied externally or that auxiliary bias loop isn’t required for basic differential amplification, M15 can be removed. impact_estimate: Low if net043 is externally set or the auxiliary loop is non-essential; high if it is required to bias the main mirror/tail
